intended_object: An auxiliary R-linear operator giving one particular choice of quotient coordinates when a restricted power series f is divided by restricted divisors g_i that agree with polynomial divisors b_i modulo I. It is built as (fixed polynomial-division quotient map) ∘ (Neumann-series inverse of id − error operator). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: This is a proof device, not a standard mathematical object. It composes the library's fixed polynomial division-quotient operator (`restrictedDivisionQuotient`) with the geometric (Neumann-series) inverse of id − E. Here E is the error operator x ↦ Σ_i q_i(x)·(b_i − g_i), whose terms are the quotients q_i(x) times the gap between the polynomial and the actual divisors. The output depends on the arbitrary choices made inside the fixed polynomial division operators. The module documentation of the next definition, `restrictedPerturbedDivisionRemainder`, says explicitly: "No independence from division choices or uniqueness is asserted". So this is not the canonical quotient of a Weierstrass/Gröbner-type division theorem. It is an intermediate construction used to prove the decomposition f = Σ q_i g_i + r, where r has zero coefficients in every leading cone. The construction is coherent for that purpose. Composing the two operators and the decomposition proof make sense. But there is no literature object to compare it with.
